fatal_errors: Does not identify the specific AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA.
Substitutes high-pressure/high-temperature processing for intermediate-temperature thermal aging.
Predicts simultaneous strength and ductility enhancement rather than a non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition.
Omits the critical 600°C embrittlement and 750°C ductility-recovery conditions.
Omits L12 ordering, elevated antiphase-boundary energy, planar slip, and jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries.
The cited evidence concerns HPHT-induced strength-ductility synergy and nanowire plasticity, not temper embrittlement in the target alloy.
The proposed falsification experiment cannot distinguish the target phase-boundary-mediated embrittlement mechanism from generic mechanical-property changes.
explanation: The response only broadly aligns with the topic by discussing high-entropy alloys and contrasting them with conventional temper-embrittled alloys. It reconstructs a different study concerning HPHT-induced strength-ductility synergy. It neither identifies the eutectic AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy nor describes the aging-temperature-dependent ductile-brittle-ductile transition. The decisive structural and mechanistic features—maximized L12 ordering and jagged B2/FCC boundaries near 600°C, followed by reduced ordering and ductile transition zones near 750°C—are absent. Although the citations support the unrelated HPHT claims, they do not provide relevant evidence for the requested transition.
